scripts.radio:
Hamjambo wasikilizaji, and welcome back to Kenya on Record. Today, we need to talk plainly about public money and where it actually goes.

This week, the government announced an audit of all public sector workers across ministries, departments, and counties. Why now? Because an astounding 6.2 billion shillings has slipped through the cracks—paid out directly to ghost workers. That is over six billion shillings disbursed to non-existent employees, people who never set foot in an office, or names kept deliberately on the payroll by syndicates manipulating public systems.

Let us put that figure into perspective. Six point two billion shillings is not just a budget line item. That is enough money to stock hundreds of dispensaries with essential medication, hire thousands of desperately needed junior secondary teachers, or build permanent classrooms. Instead, it vanishes into private accounts every single month while citizens are squeezed harder through taxes.

An audit is a start, but an audit alone is not accountability. We have had headcounts before, biometric registration drives, and special task forces. What matters is what happens after the names are scrubbed. The officials who signed off on those vouchers, the HR officers who maintained those lists, and the bank accounts that received that public cash must face the law. Recovery of the money must follow.

Kwa ufupi: Serikali imeanza ukaguzi wa wafanyikazi wote wa umma baada ya shilingi bilioni sita nukta mbili kupotea kupitia wafanyikazi hewa. Pesa hizi za umma zinafaa kurejeshwa, na wahusika wote wachukuliwe hatua kali za kisheria mara moja.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu, hope your week is moving well. Just dropping a quick update here from Kenya on Record because this ghost worker story needs our full attention.

The state is finally conducting a comprehensive audit of all public service staff. Why? Over 6.2 billion shillings has been stolen through ghost worker payroll fraud. Think about that number for a minute. That is 6.2 billion shillings of our tax money going to imaginary people, while civil servants who actually show up struggle with delayed allowances, and public clinics run out of basic supplies.

Every time we are told the government has no money for critical services, remember this: the resources exist, but the leakages are massive. We will be tracking this audit closely to ensure it doesn't just end with another report gathering dust. Demand names, demand prosecutions. Tuanze hapo.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Sh6.2B lost to ghost workers is money stolen from hospitals and schools. If someone on your local payroll never shows up to work, report it to EACC.
scripts.reels:
Six point two billion shillings. That is what ghost workers have cost Kenyan taxpayers.

Now, the government is launching a nationwide audit of every public employee. But we have to ask the hard question: who was approving these payrolls month after month?

Ghost workers don't create themselves—corrupt officials do. An audit without arrests and full asset recovery is just public relations.

Follow Kenya on Record. We follow the paper trail.
